title: 📝️ semio repo todos
$comment: 🧬️ The wire contract of the 📝️todos module: a todo is a line of source rather than a stored document, so the shapes here are the todo a scan yields, the draft a store keeps, and the fixture files under 🧫️fixtures that state the trees, the lines and the scripts every implementation replays.

Location.$comment: 📍️ Where a todo lives: the file, the one based line and the one based column. A todo appended to a file has line 0 until the next scan reads it back.

Todo.$comment: ✅️ One todo. The identifier is the slug of the name, the parent is the directory whose `.todos.md` carries it or the file whose comment it is.

Draft.$comment: 🎨️ One draft: a directory of copied files under the repository's notes tree, addressed by the slug of its title.

TreeFile.$comment: 📄️ One file of a stated tree: a `/` separated path relative to the scan root and the exact text at that path.

ScanTreeVectors.$comment: 🔍️ 🧫️fixtures/🔍️scan-tree.json — a whole tree stated as its own files, covering every branch a scan has to answer for: a directory `.todos.md`, todo comments in each supported extension and comment opener, an unsupported extension, a skipped directory, a dotted directory, an item with no description, a description carrying colons and a comment that only looks like a todo. These are specification vectors, not recorded data: this checkout carries no `.todos.md` at all, which the no-oracle decision states.

LineVectors.$comment: 📝️ 🧫️fixtures/📝️line-vectors.json — the two documents a todo can live in and the rewrites applied to them. `markdown` is a whole `.todos.md`, `source` is a whole commented file, and each rewrite names the line it touches and what it becomes, so a round trip re-parses what a rewrite wrote.

TodoStep.$comment: 🎬️ One step of the todo lifecycle script. `op` is `create`, `change`, `delete`, `to-ticket`, `find` or `list`; `input` carries whatever that operation reads.

TodoScript.$comment: 🎫️ 🧫️fixtures/🔓️lifecycle-script.json — one ordered history over an in-memory tree, ticket opener and emitter, including the refusals a caller has to get back.

DraftStep.$comment: 🎬️ One step of the draft script. `op` is `create`, `delete` or `list`.

DraftScript.$comment: ✏️ 🧫️fixtures/✏️draft-script.json — one ordered history over an in-memory draft store, including a title carrying no slug, a duplicate identifier and a removal of a draft that never existed.
